fields.label: Slab
fields.description: Which slab this benefit belongs to. Several rows carrying the same slab number are one slab granting a combo - five percent off and a free case together - so the slab number, not the row number, is what the engine matches and what a rep and a manager argue about later.

fields.label: From
fields.description: Where the slab opens, inclusive, in the units the parent measures: cases or pieces on a quantity scheme, rupees on a value one. Rows sharing a slab number must agree on this.

fields.label: To
fields.description: Where the slab closes, inclusive. Ignored on the top slab, where Open Top is ticked instead.

fields.label: Open Top
fields.description: The slab has no ceiling. A Float column in Frappe is never null, so a blank To reads back as zero and a slab meant to run to infinity would instead close at nothing; this flag is the only thing that tells the two apart. Exactly one slab may carry it, and it must be the highest.

fields.label: Benefit
fields.options:
Free Goods
Percent Discount
Value Discount
Rate Off
Incentive
fields.description: What this row grants, and therefore which single column below it is allowed to carry a number. Incentive is money for the rep: it is accrued and reported on its own, and never comes off the shop bill, because counting it as a discount overstates what the shopkeeper was given and turns into an argument at claim settlement.

fields.label: Per
fields.description: How often the benefit is granted. Slab grants it once on crossing the line; Unit grants it on every qualifying unit; Multiple grants it again at every whole multiple of the slab floor, which is how buy-ten-get-one repeats at twenty.

fields.label: Free Item
fields.description: What is given away. It may be a different SKU from the one that qualified - a soap scheme that pays out in sachets is ordinary - and it bills at zero without ever re-entering a basis, so a free case can never help the cart cross the next slab.

fields.label: Free Qty
fields.description: How much is given away each time the benefit is granted, counted in the unit beside it.

fields.label: Free Unit
fields.description: The unit the free quantity is typed in. One free piece and one free case are the same number on this row and a very different conversation at delivery, so the unit is recorded rather than assumed.

fields.label: Discount %
fields.description: Taken off the qualifying lines only, never off the whole cart - a five percent soap scheme must not be seen to have discounted the tea. The compiler turns this into basis points so the engine can do it in whole numbers.

fields.label: Value Discount
fields.description: A flat sum off the bill, in rupees.

fields.label: Rate Off
fields.description: Rupees off each unit. Typed per case where the scheme was written per case; the compiler restates it per base unit so the engine never divides.

fields.label: Incentive
fields.description: Rupees to the rep, not off the shop bill. It accrues to the scheme ledger and is paid through payout, which is why it is kept apart from every other column here.

fields.label: Reads As
fields.description: This row in the words a rep would use at a counter. A slab table is unreadable to someone standing in front of a shopkeeper who is already serving the next customer.
